question: Should OpenClaw adopt this private localization-core package and its locale-precedence contract as the shared foundation for the linked five-part localization series?
rationale: The patch defines cross-surface runtime ownership and compatibility semantics that later CLI, Gateway, approval, and channel work will inherit; this cannot be resolved safely as a mechanical contributor follow-up.

options.title: Sponsor the shared contract
options.body: Approve the runtime boundary and precedence model, then require the contributor to remove the changelog entry and supply live proof before normal review continues.

options.title: Narrow the first slice
options.body: Limit this PR to the approved foundation consumers and defer Gateway/approval or process-wide CLI adoption until their owners agree on the contract.

options.title: Pause the series
options.body: Hold the stacked localization branches until the RFC records an accepted core-versus-surface ownership direction.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the shared contract
recommendation.body: Approve the runtime boundary and precedence model, then require the contributor to remove the changelog entry and supply live proof before normal review continues.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the available author of the linked localization RFC and original foundation work, so they can clarify the proposed contract while an OpenClaw owner makes the acceptance decision.
